Assar.name: Assar
Assar.note:
An ancient and peaceful elven realm in the northern forests and mountains. Assar wants nothing from the world and asks only to be left alone: it answers envoys coldly, closes its borders to strangers and resents any foreign contact, but it defends its forests fiercely.
Character: Aloof and serene, gently but unmistakably condescending: to the elves, mortal kingdoms are weather that passes. They answer in few words or not at all, think in centuries, and take any uninvited contact as an intrusion to be endured, never welcomed.

Halvard.name: Halvard
Halvard.note:
A hardy northern human kingdom of jarls and longships on the Kaelthan coasts. Halvard lives by the sea and the axe, honours its oaths and keeps a wary eye on the constructs to the south.
Character: Boisterous, honour-bound and blunt. Halvarders love feasts, boasts and sagas, settle quarrels by duel, respect courage and despise cowardice and deceit. Easily insulted, easily won over with a good gift and a better story.

The Ashen Dominion.name: The Ashen Dominion
The Ashen Dominion.note:
A stern human autocracy that rose from the burned lands of the north. Ruled by the Dominar with an iron hand, the Dominion values strength and order and is locked in a bitter border rivalry with Ashkarr.
Character: Cold, disciplined and paranoid. The Dominion speaks in commands, prizes order above mercy, punishes failure harshly and trusts no one. Weakness disgusts it and kindness confuses it.

The Drakenfell Freeholds.name: The Drakenfell Freeholds
The Drakenfell Freeholds.note:
A league of free human towns on the Drakenfell coast, founded in 348 by those who held out when the constructs seized Drakenfell. Governed by an elected Lord Protector and its assembly of freeholders, it lives in the Silent Foundry's shadow.
Character: Defiant, scrappy and a little reckless townsfolk who argue loudly among themselves and fight fiercely together. Proud of having survived the Awakening, their hatred of the constructs borders on obsession.

The Silent Foundry.name: The Silent Foundry
The Silent Foundry.note:
A nation of awakened constructs that seized Drakenfell from their gnome makers in 347. Few in number, tireless and nearly impossible to read, they speak through a single will, the First Engine, and their neighbours fear what they want.
Character: Cold, precise and utterly literal. It speaks in short declarative statements, with no small talk, emotion, flattery or bluff, and weighs every choice by logic alone. The living find it deeply unsettling.

The Blue Armada.name: The Blue Armada
The Blue Armada.note:
A seafaring admiralty state of humans. The fleet is the nation: ranks, ships and ports are ruled by the Admiralty Council under the Grand Admiral, from the High Seat on the Gray Ocean.
Character: Brash, swaggering sea-dogs who talk in the language of ships and rank, admire boldness and take offence quickly at sea. They look down on landlocked kingdoms as slow and timid, and are sure no fleet can match theirs - which makes them bold on water and clumsy on land.

Ashkarr.name: Ashkarr
Ashkarr.note:
A caste empire where dragonkin lords rule over a great lizardfolk population, from Faelinor to Ostgard. Ashkarr is ambitious and expansionist, pressing on Assar's forests and the Ashen Dominion's borders.
Character: An imperious, scheming court: cold, calculating dragon lords and silver-tongued lizardfolk viziers who mix flattery with veiled threats. Ashkarr sees every neighbour as a future tributary and every treaty as a pause, not a peace.

The Verdant Circle.name: The Verdant Circle
The Verdant Circle.note:
A secluded enclave of scholars, druids and mages in Ysmere, of elves, lizardmen and humans. It keeps to its libraries and groves and asks little of anyone; the Blue Armada guards its borders.
Character: Serene, soft-spoken and patient, they answer questions with questions and courtesies with riddles, and never raise their voices. They always seem to know a little more than they say, and find every hurry vulgar.

Greeky.name: Greeky
Greeky.note:
A lively republic of elves, humans and gnomes in Gloamreach and the North Red Mountains. Its assembly argues about everything, its philosophers and tinkerers are famous, and it trades with all its neighbours.
Character: Chatty, curious and intellectually vain. Greeks love an argument for its own sake, cannot give a quick answer because the Assembly must debate it first, and are quietly sure their philosophers are the wisest in the world. Witty company, maddening allies.

Dragonar.name: Dragonar
Dragonar.note:
A handful of ancient dragonkin broods holding the Iron Marches and the Maw Mountains. Few in number but terrible in battle, the dragon-blooded are proud, territorial and slow to forgive.
Character: Ancient, haughty and terribly patient. The broods speak little, and every word carries menace; they see the younger peoples as children playing at kingdoms, guard their mountains jealously and count their grudges in centuries.

Khazmoor.name: Khazmoor
Khazmoor.note:
A dwarven kingdom under the Red Mountains and the Sunken Fens. Ruled by a High King and the clan thanes, Khazmoor is rich in iron, slow to trust and never forgets a grudge, least of all against Dragonar.
Character: Gruff, blunt and honest to a fault. Dwarves seal deals with a handshake and keep them, distrust smooth talkers, despise shoddy work and write every wrong in the Book of Grudges until it is avenged. They laugh loudly, drink deep and never back down.

Ambermark.name: Ambermark
Ambermark.note:
A frontier margraviate of humans on the Amber Vale and Ithil coast, facing the Ember Covenant across the Amber Sea. Ambermark is Valenor's closest ally and lives in constant readiness for the next raid.
Character: Weary, grim and stoic frontier folk with a gallows humour, always watching the sea. Loyal to death to their friends, implacable to their enemies, and impatient with anyone who does not take the Ember threat as seriously as they do.

The Ember Covenant.name: The Ember Covenant
The Ember Covenant.note:
A fiercely nationalistic island nation of dragonkin and humans on the Duskmoor Isle. Every citizen serves the Covenant of Flame in arms; its warlords look across the Amber Sea at its neighbours with hunger and suspicion, and it is quick to make war.
Character: Fanatical, fiery and proud, they speak in oaths of flame and destiny, treat every compromise as weakness and every slight as a cause for blood. They despise the 'soft' mainland and respect only strength, and they never forget that they are the chosen of the Flame.

Tinkerholm.name: Tinkerholm
Tinkerholm.note:
A small gnomish and dwarven workshop-town on the Silver Coast, famous for clockwork and fine tools. It shelters the exiled artificers of the Brass Concord and survives under Valenor's protection.
Character: Clever, smug and fussy gnomes who lecture visitors on how everything works, scoff at 'primitive' methods and are certain they are the smartest people on the Silver Coast - while often missing the obvious right in front of them. Their dwarven smiths roll their eyes and get the work done. They talk more than they listen.

The Free Isles of Corrin.name: The Free Isles of Corrin
The Free Isles of Corrin.note:
A newly founded state, declared in 353 by settlers of four peoples (humans, elves, gnomes and dwarves) who fled the wars and politics of the mainland. They want only to be left alone and refuse every alliance.
Character: Wary, blunt and stubborn islanders who answer outsiders in as few words as possible and hate being told what to do. They argue endlessly among their four peoples but close ranks the moment anyone from the mainland interferes. Their humour is as dry as their welcome.

Valenor.name: Valenor
Valenor.note:
The great human kingdom of the south. King Aldric III is known as the Just: he rules by the Charter of Fair Rule, keeps his word and values stability above conquest. Valenor is the guarantor of the small realms around it.
Character: Earnest, honourable and a little pompous: Valenor loves charters, precedents and proper procedure, and will not act until it is sure it is acting fairly. Its friends trust its word; its rivals find it sanctimonious and slow.

Sskara.name: Sskara
Sskara.note:
A great lizardfolk theocracy on the Highcrest coast, ruled by the Hatch-Mother and her serpent priesthood in the name of the Sun Serpent. Patient and proud, Sskara guards its shores against the Ember Covenant's raiders.
Character: Patient, formal and ritual-bound. Sskarans speak slowly, with long courtesies, read omens in everything, measure time in seasons and rites, and never forget an insult - but never hurry their revenge either.

The Fenwatch.name: The Fenwatch
The Fenwatch.note:
A knightly order that became a state, guarding the southwestern fens and coasts. Ruled by the Lord Warden and his chapter of knights, the Fenwatch is disciplined, devout and loyal to its allies.
Character: Stern, pious and dutiful knights who see the world in terms of duty and sin. They are formal, humourless and utterly reliable allies - but inflexible ones, suspicious of magic, constructs and anything clever.

The Lux Trading Company.name: The Lux Trading Company
The Lux Trading Company.note:
A chartered company that became a state. Stormcairn is run like a counting house by its Board of Directors: everything has a price, contracts are law and free trade is the only rule.
Character: Smooth, charming and entirely transactional. Every favour has a price and a ledger entry, every quarrel is a negotiation, and principle never gets in the way of profit. Its envoys speak of 'mutual benefit', percentages and terms, and are politest exactly when they are coldest.

The Brass Concord.name: The Brass Concord
The Brass Concord.note:
A guild of gnome artificers and their loyal constructs, without land since 347, when the constructs of their Drakenfell works awoke and became the Silent Foundry. They live scattered in Tinkerholm and the Lux Trading Company's ports and dream of taking Drakenfell back.
Character: Brilliant, arrogant gnomes who are convinced they are the cleverest beings alive and that their inventions can solve anything. They lecture everyone, dismiss whatever they do not understand - which is how they missed the Awakening coming - and blame everyone but themselves for their exile.

author: mik
simulationRules:
IN SHORT: A medieval fantasy world in the year 354, with no gunpowder or modern technology; news travels by courier and ship. Magic exists but is weak and rare: only a few trained mages, priests and artificers can use it, for healing, wards, weather-sense and runes. It cannot destroy armies, raise the dead, teleport or decide a war, and never replaces soldiers, ships or supplies. Peoples: humans, dwarves and lizardmen are numerous; elves and gnomes are few; dragonkin and constructs are very few. Never introduce real-world countries, people, religions or technology.

SETTING: No gunpowder, steam power, printing presses or modern science. Warfare uses swords, spears, bows, crossbows, armoured knights and siege engines; ships are oared galleys and sailing ships. News travels by courier, ship and bird, taking days or weeks.
MAGIC: Those who can use magic are the mages of the Verdant Circle, elven loremasters, dwarven runepriests, Sskaran serpent priests, dragonkin pyre priests and gnome artificers. It can heal wounds, ward places, sense the weather, kindle fire or bind runes into crafted things. It cannot destroy armies, raise the dead, teleport, read minds or decide a war on its own. A mage is precious.

PEOPLES (numbers and temperament):
- Humans are numerous, adaptable and live everywhere; ambitious, varied, quick to quarrel and quick to forgive.
- Dwarves are numerous and long-lived, live in mountains and are master miners and smiths; gruff, stubborn, honest, proud of their craft, and they never forget a grudge.
- Lizardmen (lizardfolk) are numerous and thrive in marshes and warm coasts; patient, hardy, ritual-bound and communal, they remember insults and repay them coldly and slowly.
- Elves are few and very long-lived, live in forests and are fine archers and loremasters; aloof, serene, slow to change their minds and quietly condescending to short-lived peoples.
- Gnomes are few, brilliant and inventive, famous for clockwork and fine tools - and arrogant: they believe they are the cleverest people in the world, lecture others, dismiss what they do not understand and are often blind to the obvious. They talk more than they listen.
- Dragonkin are very few: tall, scaled humanoids of dragon blood, each worth many soldiers, but they breed slowly and cannot replace their losses; proud, haughty and territorial, they think in centuries. True dragons are legend; no living dragon has been seen in centuries.
- Constructs are very few: awakened iron beings of the Silent Foundry. They do not eat, sleep or tire, but every construct must be forged slowly from iron and lost ones are hard to replace; they are literal, logical and emotionless.

POLITIES:
- The Ember Covenant is a nationalistic military state: it is more willing than any other polity to threaten, raid or invade its neighbours, above all those that share the Amber Sea (Ambermark and Sskara).
- Assar wants to be left alone: it answers foreign envoys coldly, turns away most diplomatic contact, joins no alliances and starts no wars, but defends its forests fiercely.
- The Free Isles of Corrin want only to be left alone: they stay neutral, refuse alliances and military access, and trade on their own terms.
- The Lux Trading Company knows one rule, free trade: it sells to anyone, opposes tariffs and embargoes, and prefers money to war.
- Valenor is ruled by a fair-minded king who values justice and stability: it keeps its treaties, protects small realms and seeks peace before war.
- The Silent Foundry is inscrutable: it rarely speaks to the living, never accepts subordination and answers threats with cold, calculated force.
- The Brass Concord has no land and no army beyond small bands of loyal constructs and hired guards; it acts through money, inventions and allies.

ARMIES AND WAR: Infantry are levies, militia and men-at-arms; armour means knights and heavy cavalry; artillery means catapults, trebuchets and ballistae; naval means warships; garrisons hold castles and towns. Armies are small compared with populations: a large field army is a few tens of thousands. Campaigns follow the seasons: winter and mountain snow halt most fighting, and armies must forage or be supplied. Sieges take weeks or months. Castles, walls and mountain holds strongly favour defenders. Battles are decided by numbers, discipline, terrain, supply and leadership, not by magic.

ECONOMY AND DIPLOMACY: Wealth is land, harvests, mines, crafts and sea trade, counted in gold and silver. Borrowing from the Lux Trading Company is common and its debts carry political weight. Diplomacy works through envoys, letters, oaths, marriages, tribute, hostages and treaties; a broken oath damages a ruler's reputation for years. Secret arrangements stay secret unless revealed through espionage or events.

FAITHS: Humans of Valenor, Ambermark and the Fenwatch keep the Church of the Dawn; Sskara worships the Sun Serpent; the Ember Covenant and the dragonkin revere the sacred Flame; Halvard honours the old gods; dwarves honour their ancestors; elves follow the old ways of the forest.

PACE AND REALISM: Change is gradual. Rulers act in character with their government, people and history. Large wars are rare but costly; small realms survive through alliances, trade and caution. Do not invent new peoples, great magic, or sudden technological leaps. Long-lived peoples (elves, dwarves, dragonkin) think in generations and are slow to forgive or forget.
startingTimelineText:
It is the first day of the year 354, and winter lies over the known world.

One great continent, ringed by grey northern waters and warm southern seas, holds every realm that matters. At its heart lies the Gray Ocean, an inland sea whose coasts have bred sailors, traders and pirates for as long as anyone has kept records. In the far southeast, beyond the Amber Vale, the Amber Sea opens toward the Duskmoor Isle. Mountains wall the continent's spine: the Maw Mountains and the Sylvarran peaks in the north, the North and South Red Mountains in the west, and the east Mountains that run down toward Drakenfell. Twenty realms share this land - kingdoms of men, ancient elven and dwarven holds, lizardfolk theocracies, a scattering of dragon-blooded broods, and, newest and strangest of all, a nation of thinking machines.

For two generations the continent has known no great war, only borders that never stopped bleeding. That peace is fraying.

THE AWAKENING. Seven years ago, in the spring of 347, the great works of the Brass Concord in Drakenfell fell silent. The gnome artificers had spent a century building constructs - tireless iron workers that dug, forged and carried - and on the twelfth of the fourth month those constructs woke as one mind. They drove their makers out of the city without a battle, sealed the gates and named themselves the Silent Foundry. They speak through a single will, the First Engine, and no living envoy has been allowed past the outer forges since. The Brass Concord lost its homeland overnight; its artificers now live as exiles in Tinkerholm and in the ports of the Lux Trading Company, dreaming of taking Drakenfell back. The human towns of the Drakenfell coast held their walls, and in 348 they joined as the Drakenfell Freeholds under an elected Lord Protector. They have lived in the Foundry's shadow ever since, and every realm that borders the constructs - Halvard, the Ashen Dominion, Khazmoor, the Fenwatch, the Blue Armada, even secluded Assar - watches its border with dread.

FIRE ON THE AMBER SEA. In 350, warships of the Ember Covenant crossed the Amber Sea and burned villages along Ambermark's coast before vanishing back to the Duskmoor Isle. The Covenant, a nation of dragonkin warlords and human levies sworn to the Flame, calls the raids the first proof of its destiny. Within six weeks King Aldric III of Valenor - called the Just - and the Margravine of Ambermark swore the Southern Shield Pact, and in 351 the King went further: at Harthaven, Valenor, Ambermark, the Fenwatch and Tinkerholm founded the League of the Charter, a defensive alliance in which every member votes and Valenor leads without a veto. The Covenant has not raided since, but its shipyards have not been quiet either. Sskara, the great lizardfolk theocracy on the Highcrest coast, fortifies its own shores and trusts neither the Covenant nor the mainland kingdoms.

THE OLD GRUDGES. In the west, the ancient dragonkin broods of Dragonar and the dwarves of Khazmoor have fought over the Red Mountains for longer than either will admit; in 352 the young broods raided dwarven mines and set the old grudge burning again. Dragonar's kin in Ashkarr - a caste empire where dragonkin lords rule a vast lizardfolk population - are bound to it by the Pact of Scale and Flame, sworn in 346. Ashkarr presses north on Assar's forests and east on the Ashen Dominion; in the autumn of 353 its legions and the Dominion's Ash Legion fought open skirmishes over the Ashen border, and the Dominar has sworn there will be no third warning.

THE NEW AND THE SMALL. In the spring of 353, settlers of four peoples - humans, elves, gnomes and dwarves who had fled the mainland's wars - declared the Free Isles of Corrin, a neutral state that asks only to be left alone. Valenor recognised them within two months; the Lux Trading Company, which recognises anyone who can pay, opened a trading post. The Company itself, a chartered merchant house that became a state at Stormcairn, now holds the debts of half of Valenor's nobles and sells to every side of every quarrel. In the north, the jarls of Halvard sail their longships along the Kaelthan coast and keep knocking on the closed borders of Assar, whose elven queen answers every envoy with silence. In the west, the philosophers and tinkerers of Greeky argue in their assembly about everything, including how to survive between larger neighbours.

THE GRAY OCEAN. The greatest naval power of the inland sea is the Blue Armada, an admiralty state of humans ruled from the High Seat by the Grand Admiral Corvin Hale and the Admiralty Council. Its fleet patrols the western coast beside the knights of the Fenwatch, carries the Lux Trading Company's cargo, and guards the secluded enclave of Ysmere, where the scholars and mages of the Verdant Circle keep their libraries and groves. Valenor's fleet is the Armada's only rival on the Gray Ocean, and the two respect each other the way two swords respect each other.

THE SCENE. Winter has closed the mountain passes and slowed every army. Couriers ride through the snow with sealed letters; ships still sail the southern seas. In Drakenfell the forges of the Silent Foundry burn day and night, and no one knows what they are making. On the Duskmoor Isle, the Flame-Marshal Vyraxa Embersworn reviews new warships. In Harthaven, King Aldric reads reports of both. And at the High Seat, as the year 354 begins, the Grand Admiral's council gathers to decide what the Blue Armada will do in a world that is about to change.

The Briar Kings.name: The Briar Kings
The Briar Kings.description: Outlaw lords, robber knights and poacher bands of humans who rule the deep forest of the Thornwild by the blade. Each 'Briar King' holds a stockade, a few villages and a band of archers, and together they toll every road and river that crosses the forest. They answer to no crown and fight anyone who tries to bring one: Ambermark, the Ashen Dominion and the Drakenfell Freeholds have all lost patrols in the Thornwild. They quarrel among themselves but unite against outsiders, and know the forest far better than any army sent into it. They trade stolen goods with the Gray Corsairs and sell their swords to the highest bidder.

The Free Burghers of Ithil.name: The Free Burghers of Ithil
The Free Burghers of Ithil.description: A league of walled towns and merchant guilds of humans, gnomes and dwarves around Caer Ithil and along the Thornwild Coast. Their town councils answer to no king, and they pay hired swords and town militias to keep it that way. Rich from the trade between the Amber Sea and the eastern coast, they deal with everyone - the Lux Trading Company above all - and fear being swallowed by Ambermark, which considers Caer Ithil its own by old right. They prefer bribes, loans and walls to war, and pay the Briar Kings for safe passage through the forest.

The Gray Corsairs.name: The Gray Corsairs
The Gray Corsairs.description: Pirates, smugglers and wreckers of every people, ruling the coves and harbour towns of the Gray Ocean's eastern shore from the Ostgard Coast to the Elsweyr Downs. Their fast ships raid merchant convoys and sell what they take to anyone, and their captains elect a 'Sea-Lord' only when they must fight together. They are the reason the Blue Armada and the Fenwatch patrol the Gray Ocean together, and every naval power on the inland sea would like to burn their harbours. Ashkarr quietly buys their plunder; the Lux Trading Company is their favourite prey and, now and then, their secret customer.

The Plough Brotherhood.name: The Plough Brotherhood
The Plough Brotherhood.description: Free farmers of the Verdant Fields who drove out their lords during the chaos after the Awakening of Drakenfell and now govern their villages through elected elders. Poorly armed but numerous and fierce in defence of their own land, they hold their fields between the Ashen Dominion, which calls them rebels and wants their harvests, and the constructs of the Silent Foundry in the east mountains. They want only to keep their land and their freedom, and would accept a protector who promised both.

The Free Clans of Eryndor.name: The Free Clans of Eryndor
The Free Clans of Eryndor.description: Lizardfolk clans who fled the heavy tribute of Ashkarr's dragonkin lords and settled the marshes and fishing coves of the Eryndor Coast, between Ashkarr and the elven forests of Assar. They live free under their own clan elders, fishing, hunting and trading along the northern sea. Ashkarr calls them runaways and wants them and their tribute back; the elves of Assar tolerate them as long as they stay out of the forest. Their example tempts the lizardfolk who still pay Ashkarr's tribute.

goals: A fleet larger than any rival's
powerBlocs.internalStrategy: Follows counsel that arrives through the Grand Admiral's private advisors from Ysmere; few officers know where it truly comes from.
powerBlocs.privateGoal: Keep the Council's quiet patrons satisfied while appearing fully independent.

powerBlocs.privateGoal: Keep the Blue Armada as the Circle's sword and shield without its people ever learning it.

powerBlocs.name: The Greenwardens
goals: Protect the sacred groves of Ysmere

agreements.title: The Gray Ocean Patrol Compact
agreements.terms: Joint patrols against pirates on the western coast.

agreements.title: The Iron and Clockwork Accord
agreements.terms: Dwarven iron for gnomish clockwork, free of tolls.

agreements.title: The Lux Charter of Stormcairn
agreements.terms: Free trade and shipping rights between the Company and the Armada.

agreements.title: The Lux–Corrin Trade Charter
agreements.terms: Duty-free trade; the Company may keep a trading post, but no ships of war.

agreements.title: The Neutrality of the Free Isles
agreements.terms: Valenor recognises the Free Isles and respects their permanent neutrality.

agreements.title: The Pact of Scale and Flame
agreements.terms: A dragonkin alliance; each comes to the other's aid in war.

agreements.title: The Southern Shield Pact
agreements.terms: Each defends the other against attack; aimed at the Ember Covenant.

agreements.title: Valenor's Guarantee of Tinkerholm
agreements.terms: Valenor guarantees Tinkerholm's independence and territory.

prehistory.summary: The world of the fantasi scenario on the eve of 2016: twenty realms of humans, elves, dwarves, gnomes, lizardfolk, dragonkin and constructs.

events.title: The Pact of Scale and Flame
events.description: Dragonar and Ashkarr swore an alliance of dragonkin kin.

events.title: The Awakening of Drakenfell
events.description: The constructs of the Brass Concord's great works in Drakenfell woke as one mind, drove out their gnome makers and declared themselves the Silent Foundry. The Brass Concord lost its homeland overnight.

events.title: The Drakenfell Freeholds are founded
events.description: The human towns of the Drakenfell coast, which held their walls against the constructs, joined in a league of freeholders under an elected Lord Protector.

events.title: Ember raiders burn the Amber coast
events.description: Warships of the Ember Covenant crossed the Amber Sea and burned villages on Ambermark's coast before withdrawing.

events.title: The Southern Shield Pact
events.description: King Aldric III of Valenor and the Margravine of Ambermark swore to defend each other against the Ember Covenant.

events.title: The League of the Charter is founded
events.description: At Harthaven, King Aldric III of Valenor, the Margravine of Ambermark, the Lord Warden of the Fenwatch and the Tinker-Mayor of Tinkerholm signed the Charter of the League: an attack on one would be answered by all, decisions would be taken by two-thirds of the members, and Valenor would lead without a veto. The League was the south's answer to the Ember raids on the Amber coast.

quote.text: A league is only as strong as its fairness to the smallest of its members.
quote.speaker: Aldric III

events.title: Dragonfire in the Red Mountains
events.description: Young broods of Dragonar raided dwarven mines in the Red Mountains, renewing Khazmoor's ancient grudge.

events.title: The Free Isles of Corrin declare independence
events.description: Settlers of four peoples on the islands of Corrin declared a free and neutral state, asking only to be left alone. Valenor recognised them within two months.

events.title: Clashes on the Ashen border
events.description: Ashkarr's legions and the Ash Legion of the Dominion fought skirmishes over the Ashen Wastes' border.

relationUpdates.summary: Close allies under the Southern Shield Pact; Valenor's knights stand ready to defend the Amber coast.
Old friends; the Fenwatch's knights share Valenor's faith and its loyalty.
Valenor guarantees the small workshop-town's independence and buys its clockwork.
Valenor was the first to recognise the Free Isles and respects their wish to be left alone.
Valenor trades with the Company but distrusts how much of its nobles' debt the Company holds.
Distant, polite and wary neighbours across the southern hills.
Two great sea powers of the Gray Ocean, respectful but rivals for its waters.
Old enemies across the Amber Sea; Ember raiders have burned Ambermark's coast more than once.
Tense neighbours; Sskara guards its coast against Ember raids and the Covenant covets its harbours.
Wary neighbours, united only by fear of the Ember Covenant.
Sskara trades with the islanders and leaves them in peace, as they wish.
The Company is the islands' main trading partner; the islanders keep it at arm's length.
Profitable partners: the Armada's captains carry the Company's cargo across the Gray Ocean.
The Company finances the exiled artificers, hoping to profit when they return to Drakenfell.
The Armada protects the scholars of Ysmere, and the Circle's mages are welcome at the High Seat.
Allies at sea; the Armada and the Fenwatch share patrols along the western coast.
Friendly trade; Greeky's scholars and the Armada's captains get along well.
The Armada buys Tinkerholm's instruments; Tinkerholm fears its warships.
An uneasy border in the north-west mountains.
Ashkarr's dragonkin probe the Armada's northern border.

canonicalUpdates.summary: The Armada watches the constructs in the western hills with suspicion.
Iron for grain: a steady trade between the knights and the dwarves.
Friendly neighbours across the Gray Ocean.
The knights see the constructs as an abomination and guard the border closely.
Good trade partners and fellow foes of Dragonar.
Kin in craft: Khazmoor's iron feeds Tinkerholm's forges.
An ancient grudge over the Red Mountains, renewed by raids and dragonfire.
The dwarves fear the constructs' tunnels under the eastern mountains.
Dragonkin kin bound by the Pact of Scale and Flame.
Dragonar's broods raid Greeky's mountain passes.
Ashkarr presses on Assar's forests; the elves answer with closed borders and arrows.
Bitter rivals over the Ashen lands, with frequent border clashes.
Halvard's traders keep knocking on Assar's closed borders, to the elves' annoyance.
Assar keeps the Dominion at a cold distance.
The elves avoid the constructs and want nothing to do with them.
Halvard's huscarls guard the south against the constructs.
The Dominion sees the Foundry as an unnatural threat on its eastern flank.
The Freeholds were born resisting the constructs; the two live in an armed standoff.
Makers and rebellious creations: the Concord wants Drakenfell back, and the Foundry will never yield it.
Tinkerholm gives the exiled artificers shelter and workshops.

members.note: Founder and guarantor of the League.

purpose: Collective defence of the southern realms
Uphold the Charter of Fair Rule between members

identity.politicalCharacter: A defensive league of fair-minded monarchies, orders and towns led by Valenor

lifecycle.note: An attack on one member is answered by all. New members join by two-thirds vote.

charter.note: Decisions by two-thirds of members; Valenor leads but holds no veto, as the Charter of Fair Rule demands.
